steps.instruction: Download and install Git for your system.
Open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds Git and shows its version.

name: ESP-IDF
summary: Espressif's framework for building and flashing ESP32 firmware.

steps.instruction: Install ESP-IDF using Espressif's installer for your system.
steps.expect: The installer finishes and adds an ESP-IDF terminal.

steps.instruction: Start this app from the ESP-IDF terminal so it can find the tools, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds idf.py and shows its version.

name: PlatformIO
summary: Builds and flashes firmware for many boards.

steps.expect: The install command finishes without errors.

steps.instruction: Open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds pio and shows its version.

name: Arduino CLI
summary: Command-line builds and uploads for Arduino-compatible boards.

steps.expect: The arduino-cli program is on your system.

steps.instruction: Open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds arduino-cli and shows its version.

name: KiCad
summary: Open-source circuit and PCB design, with rule checks from the command line.

steps.instruction: Add KiCad's bin folder to your PATH, open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds kicad-cli and shows its version.

steps.instruction: Install ngspice and add it to your PATH.
steps.expect: The ngspice program is on your system.

steps.instruction: Open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds ngspice and shows its version.

name: FreeCAD
summary: Open-source CAD that can be scripted without opening its window.

steps.instruction: Add FreeCAD's bin folder to your PATH, open a new terminal, then press Check.
steps.expect: The app finds freecadcmd and shows its version.

name: Fusion
summary: Fusion's built-in MCP server, which runs on this computer while Fusion is open.

steps.instruction: Open Fusion. Go to Preferences, General, API, tick Fusion MCP Server (runs locally on this device), and note the port shown there. Update Fusion if the option is missing.
steps.expect: The option is ticked and you can see the port number.

steps.instruction: Open a document in Fusion. Then enter the port under Connect Fusion on this page and press Connect.
steps.expect: Fusion appears under Connected as Healthy.

name: SolidWorks
summary: Connect a community MCP server if you trust it, or exchange STEP files by hand.

steps.instruction: Choose a community MCP server after reviewing its code, or use STEP file exchange.
steps.expect: You've picked a route you're comfortable with.

steps.instruction: If you're using a server, add it under Add an MCP server. It can break across SolidWorks versions.
steps.expect: The server's tools are listed, or you've chosen file exchange.
